chosen.chosen: The extensions of each of the six types (for example dmg, pkg, deb, rpm and appimage as Installers), read from the last part of the name after a dot, upper or lower case alike, so backup.tar.gz is an archive.
chosen.why: AC1 says the types are told apart by extension but not which ones; these are the common download formats on macOS and Linux, and ignoring case keeps PHOTO.JPG from being left out.

chosen.chosen: Each run prints a first line naming the folder in full, one line per file in name order (`would move NAME -> TYPE/`, `moved NAME -> TYPE/`, or `not moved NAME` with its reason), and a last line with the counts; a plain run's last line adds `To move them, run: sort-downloads --move`, with the folder in full when one was written, only when a file would move; `Nothing to sort in FOLDER` is printed alone only when no file gets a line.
chosen.why: AC1 asks for a list giving each file's type folder or why it stays; the full folder name lets the user see which folder (AC3) is sorted, the hint naming the given folder keeps following it from sorting ~/Downloads instead, and a folder of only untyped files still shows why each stays.

chosen.chosen: Folders and hidden files (names starting with a dot) get no line and are never moved.
chosen.why: AC2 leaves them where they were and AC1 does not ask to list them; a line for `.DS_Store` and every type folder already there would bury the files the user reads the list for.

chosen.chosen: A run told to move makes a type folder only when a file first goes into it, asks nothing before moving, and leaves in place a file it cannot move, saying `cannot move: REASON`, while the others are still sorted; a type folder name taken by a file is shown in both runs, while a refusal by the system such as no permission shows only in the run told to move, the plain run giving that file `would move`.
chosen.why: The user decided that --move is how they tell it to move, so a second yes adds nothing; empty type folders would add clutter; one file that cannot move should not stop the rest nor be lost; and a plain run that moves nothing cannot learn that the system would refuse a move.

chosen.chosen: For a folder that is not there, an unknown option, or more than one folder, the tool prints a one-line message and `Usage: sort-downloads [--move] [folder]`, and moves nothing.
chosen.why: The user's decisions give one optional folder and one option; a mistyped folder or option must not sort a folder the user did not mean, and the usage line shows the right form.

chosen.chosen: Three key results in this order: files kept whole (KR1.1), files found in their type folder (KR1.2), and lists told true (KR1.3).
chosen.why: G1 says no file is ever deleted, renamed or overwritten and that a file is found by opening its type folder; a lost file cannot be undone while an unsorted one can still be found, and the plain run's list is what the user decides to move from.

chosen.chosen: In the figures the angle brackets around each box's kind are written as mermaid's #lt; and #gt;.
chosen.why: Mermaid would take a bare <person> as an HTML tag and drop it from the box; the entity codes show as <person> once drawn.
